name: vocoder-trailer-braam
style: blockbuster trailer sound design score, two talked voices with zero melody, endless climbing Shepard-tone riser, dry clock tick that accelerates, distorted low brass braam with long reverb tail, sub-bass boom, deep vocoded synthetic narrator voice an octave down, dialogue dry and loud above the effects, near-silence vacuum before the final line, title-card slam, cinematic car horn, headlight swoosh
exclude: singing, sung chorus, melodic lead vocal, refrain, rap, rhyme, autotune on the lad, guitar, piano ballad, EDM drop, four-on-the-floor, laughter track, comedy
lyrics:
[Intro: Shepard-tone riser begins, clock ticks quick and dry]
[Talking, no melody: British teenage lad, drunk, out of breath, giggling nervously, gabbling the line]
There's infinite versions of me. One of them gets home fine.
[Riser crests, ticks race, braam, then a vacuum of silence]
[Talking, no melody: vocoded synthetic voice, an octave down, slow, colossal, utterly sure]
There's only one.
[Massive sub impact, nothing else left]
[Outro: title-card slam, one car horn, headlights swoosh past, tail rings out]
